<reason>PRO won a close, high-quality debate by making the live choice clearer: CON conceded platforms should immediately strip a home address and fake-emergency script, then admitted no pre-order actor is obliged to do so. That left CON’s alternative lagging the swarm while families absorb the raid. PRO’s kit-versus-demand line plus an express shield for leftover lawful organizing answered the mixed-campaign chill more directly than CON closed the enforcement gap. CON’s leftover point—that “throwaway brigades” stay ambiguous and overblocking remains the safer bet—was real and well-pressed, but it never displaced the core externality or CON’s own “should remove, no duty” bind.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO’s Rebuttal 2 (A4.1–A4.4): after answering CON’s pressure, the express shield for remaining organizing plus ordinary-negligence causation (omitted precaution on a controlled vector, not a cosmic counterfactual) undercut CON’s claim that a harm-based duty must bury mixed worker campaigns.</best_rebuttal>
